source.title: Commitment and Effectiveness of Situated Agents
source.venue: Proceedings of the 12th International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-91)

confidence_rationale: A foundational, empirically-measured (Tileworld) result directly relevant to the intake's own falsifiability worry (Section 12): whether ordinary intention-reconsideration policies, without any general relational topology, already suffice. It is mixed rather than a clean support/weaken: it argues FOR needing richer machinery specifically under high environmental dynamism, and AGAINST needing any extra machinery under low dynamism, where a single scalar (rate of world change) already predicts agent effectiveness well. Confidence is mid-range because it is a 1991 simplified simulated-world study (Tileworld, single-level planning) with substantial transfer risk to REE's substrate, but the finding itself is a widely-replicated cornerstone of the BDI/agent literature, not a one-off result.
failure_signatures: In the low-dynamism regime (rate of world change gamma <= ~1 in the paper's units), a 'bold' agent that never reconsiders its committed plan achieves the same effectiveness (E close to 1) as any more elaborate reconsideration strategy -- i.e. in a large, non-trivial regime of environments, ordinary hierarchical goal-following with NO reconsideration of structure at all is already optimal, which directly weakens the case that a general relational topology is NEEDED (as opposed to merely helpful) for effective behaviour in general.

The paper's entire manipulation is a single scalar environmental parameter (rate of world change) and a single scalar agent parameter (planning-steps-before-replanning); it has no representation of relation TYPES at all (no requires/enables/conflicts-with), so it cannot be read as evidence FOR the specific typed-topology extension -- only as a baseline showing how much can be explained without positing one.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Using the Tileworld testbed and the PRS real-time reasoning system, the authors varied the rate of world change (gamma) and the agent's degree of commitment (how many plan steps it executes before reconsidering). A 'bold' agent (never reconsiders mid-plan) achieves near-perfect effectiveness when gamma is low, but effectiveness drops sharply and then asymptotes toward zero as gamma increases past a threshold; a 'cautious' agent (reconsiders after every step) pays a reconsideration cost but tracks changing conditions better as dynamism rises. Which strategy wins is a simple, near-monotonic function of environmental dynamism.
mapping.ree_translation: Speaks directly to whether SD-092's existing parent/subgoal + reconsideration machinery is already sufficient without a general relational topology. In this classic result, an agent with NO stored relational structure beyond its current plan/goal -- just a policy for when to reconsider -- captures most of the qualitative behaviour the intake's Section 1 describes (sticking with a goal vs. abandoning/revising it) as a function of how often the world invalidates the current commitment. This is the strongest 'ordinary machinery may already be enough' counter-argument found in this pull, and it is exactly the failure mode the intake's own Section 12 asked to be checked for ('falsified without merely implementing a symbolic graph planner').
mapping.mapping_caveat: Gathered specifically to stress-test the NOT-YET-REGISTERED candidate claim from the sceptical side. This paper does not model a stored topology of retained possibilities at all -- reconsideration in Tileworld means re-planning from the current state, not consulting a persistent structure of previously-noticed subgoals/superordinate-goals/orthogonal options. So it cannot show the general topology is unnecessary in REE's fuller sense (which explicitly includes RETAINING low-relevance possibilities across time, e.g. MECH-292's ghost-goal bank, which Tileworld-style bold/cautious agents have no analog of). What it DOES show is that a large fraction of the 'when should I revise my commitment' behaviour is explained by a cheap scalar policy tied to environmental dynamism, which is a real burden of proof on any claim that a full multi-relation-type topology is needed for that specific sub-problem, as opposed to for the separate retention-and-later-recall sub-problem MECH-292/293 already address.
mapping.source_context: Simulated-world (Tileworld) AI planning experiment, single-level PRS reasoning agent, purely symbolic/no learning; strong internal validity (systematic parameter sweeps, reproduced in later replications by Schut & Wooldridge and others) but a simplified, discrete, single-hole-at-a-time task far removed from REE's continuous embodied substrate.

confidence_components.notes: source_quality good for its era and purpose (systematic, quantitative, foundational and widely cited/replicated in the BDI-agent literature). mapping_fidelity moderate-low: directly relevant to the reconsideration/commitment sub-question, not to the retention-of-inactive-possibilities or typed-multi-relation sub-questions. transfer_risk elevated: 1991 symbolic single-level Tileworld agent to REE's continuous, learned, multi-mechanism V3 substrate is a substantial domain jump, deliberately accepted here because the paper's VALUE is as a sceptical baseline, not as a mechanism to import directly.
